metadata.title: Weak Convergence of a Relaxed and Inertial Hybrid Projection-Proximal Point Algorithm for Maximal Monotone Operators in Hilbert Space

items.name: Resolvent and solution set
items.statement:
For a maximal monotone operator $A:H\Rightarrow H$ and $\lambda>0$, the single-valued function $J_{\lambda}^{A} := (I + \lambda A)^{-1} : H 	o H$ is the resolvent of A of parameter $\lambda$ . The resolvent is a nonexpansive mapping and, moreover,

$$
J _ {\lambda} ^ {A} (x) = x 	ext {   if   and   only   if   } 0 \in A (x). 	ag {1.2}
$$

Set $S:=A^{-1}(\{0\})$ .

items.name: Parameter assumptions (1.3)-(1.6)
items.statement:
The parameters satisfy

$$
 egin{array}{l} \lambda := \inf _ {k \geq 0} \lambda_ {k} > 0, (1.3) \  orall k \in \mathbb {N}, \alpha_ {k} \in [ 0, 1) \quad 	ext { and } \quad \alpha := \sup _ {k \geq 0} \alpha_ {k} <   1, (1.4) \ \sum \alpha_ {k} \| x ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2} <   \infty . (1.5) \ \end{array}
$$

and

$$
R _ {1} := \inf _ {k \geq 0} ho_ {k} > 0 	ext {and} R _ {2} := \sup _ {k \geq 0} ho_ {k} <   2. 	ag {1.6}
$$

items.name: Algorithm (A_1^rho)-(A_2^rho)
items.statement:
$(\mathcal{A}_1^ho)$ Given $x^{k}, x^{k-1} \in H, \lambda_k > 0$ , $\alpha_k \in [0,1)$ , and $ho_k \in (0,2)$ , find $z^k \in H$ such that

$$
(z ^ {k} - y ^ {k}) / \lambda_ {k} + v ^ {k} = \eta^ {k}, 	ext {for some} v ^ {k} \in ho_ {k} A (z ^ {k} / ho_ {k} + (1 - 1 / ho_ {k}) y ^ {k}), 	ag {2.1}
$$

where $y^{k}:= x^{k}+\alpha_{k}(x^{k}-x^{k-1})$ and the residual $\eta^k\in H$ satisfies

$$
\| \eta^ {k} \| \leq \sigma \max \{\| z ^ {k} - y ^ {k} \| / \lambda_ {k}, \| v ^ {k} \| \}. 	ag {2.2}
$$

$(\mathcal{A}_2^ho)$ If $v^{k} = 0$ then set $x^n := y^k$ for all $n \geq k + 1$ and stop.

Otherwise:

- Let $P_{k}: H 	o H$ be the orthogonal projection operator onto the hyperplane

$$
H _ {k} = \{x \in H \mid \langle v ^ {k}, x - z ^ {k} angle = (1 - 1 / ho_ {k}) \langle v ^ {k}, y ^ {k} - z ^ {k} angle \}. 	ag {2.3}
$$

- Set

$$
x ^ {k + 1} := y ^ {k} + ho_ {k} (P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k}) = y ^ {k} -  rac {\langle v ^ {k} , y ^ {k} - z ^ {k} angle}{\| v ^ {k} \| ^ {2}} v ^ {k}. 	ag {2.4}
$$

- Let $k \leftarrow k + 1$ and return to $(\mathcal{A}_1^ho)$ .

items.name: LEMMA 2.1
items.statement:
Let $\sigma \in [0,1)$ . If $v = u + \eta$ with $\| \eta \| \leq \sigma \max \{\| u\| ,\| v\|\}$ , then

(i) $\| v\| \leq \| u\| /(1 - \sigma),$  
(ii) $\langle v,uangle\geq(1-\sigma)\|u\|\|v\|$ .
items.proof: Proof. Suppose $\|v\| > \|u\|$ so that $\|\eta\| \leq \sigma \|v\|$ ; then $\|v\| \leq \|u\| + \sigma \|v\|$ , or equivalently $\|v\| \leq \|u\| / (1 - \sigma)$ ; otherwise, $\|v\| \leq \|u\|$ . In any case, (i) holds. For (ii), it suffices to consider the case $\|v\| \leq \|u\|$ [because in the complementary case $\|v\|>\|u\|$, the error bound gives $\|\eta\|\leq\sigma\|v\|$ and hence $\langle v,u\rangle=\|v\|^2-\langle v,\eta\rangle\geq(1-\sigma)\|v\|^2\geq(1-\sigma)\|u\|\|v\|$] , which implies $\langle v, u \rangle = \|u\|^2 + \langle \eta, u \rangle \geq (1 - \sigma) \|u\|^2 \geq (1 - \sigma) \|u\| \|v\|$ . ☐

items.name: LEMMA 2.3
items.statement:
Let $\varphi_k \geq 0$ and $\delta_k \geq 0$ be such that $\varphi_{k+1} \leq \varphi_k + \alpha_k (\varphi_k - \varphi_{k-1}) + \delta_k$ with $\sum \delta_k < \infty$ , and $0 \leq \alpha_k \leq \alpha < 1$ . Then the following hold:

(i) $\sum [\varphi_k - \varphi_{k-1}]_+ < \infty$ , where $[t]_+ := \max\{t, 0\}$ .  
(ii) There exists $\varphi^{*}\geq 0$ such that $\lim_{k	o \infty}\varphi_k = \varphi^*$ .
items.proof: Proof. Set $\theta_k = \varphi_k - \varphi_{k-1}$ . Then $[\theta_{k+1}]_+ \leq \alpha[\theta_k]_+ + \delta_k$ [since $\theta_{k+1}\leq\alpha_k\theta_k+\delta_k\leq\alpha[\theta_k]_+ +\delta_k$ and the right hand side is nonnegative] . This yields $[\theta_{k+1}]_+ \leq \alpha^k[\theta_1]_+ + \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} \alpha^j \delta_{k-j}$ , so that $\sum[\theta_{k+1}]_+ \leq 1/(1 - \alpha)([\theta_1]_+ + \sum \delta_k) < \infty$ . Set $w_k := \varphi_k - \sum_{j=1}^k [\theta_j]_+$ , which is bounded from below and nonincreasing [indeed $w_{k+1}-w_k=\theta_{k+1}-[\theta_{k+1}]_+\leq0$, and $w_k\geq -\sum_{j\geq1}[\theta_j]_+$ because $\varphi_k\geq0$] . It follows that $(w_k)$ is convergent; hence $\lim_{k \to \infty} \varphi_k = \sum_{j>1} [\theta_j]_+ + \lim_{k \to \infty} w_k$ .

items.name: LEMMA 2.4 (Opial)
items.statement:
Let H be a Hilbert space and $(x^{k})$ a sequence such that there exists a nonempty set $S \subset H$ verifying the following:

(a) For every $ ar{x} \in S$ , $\lim_{k 	o \infty} \|x^k -  ar{x}\|$ exists.  
(b) If $x^{k_j} ightharpoonup \hat{x}$ weakly in $H$ for a subsequence $k_j 	o \infty$ , then $\hat{x} \in S$ .

Then, there exists $x^{*} \in S$ such that $x^{k} ightharpoonup x^{*}$ weakly in $H$ as $k 	o \infty$ .
items.proof: Proof. It suffices to prove the uniqueness of the weak cluster point [existence follows because choosing any $s\in S$, condition (a) bounds $\|x^k-s\|$, and bounded sequences in a Hilbert space have weakly convergent subsequences] . The original proof in [20] requires $S$ to be closed and convex. The following argument (see [15, 22]) does not need that hypothesis. Let $\widehat{x}_1, \widehat{x}_2 \in S$ be two cluster points of $(x^k)$ for the weak topology of $H$ . Set $l_i := \lim_{k \to \infty} \|x^k - \widehat{x}_i\|^2$ for each $i = 1, 2$ . Take a sequence $k_j \to \infty$ such that $x^{k_j} \rightharpoonup \widehat{x}_1$ weakly in $H$ . But $\|x^k - \widehat{x}_1\|^2 - \|x^k - \widehat{x}_2\|^2 = \| \widehat{x}_1 - \widehat{x}_2\|^2 + 2\langle \widehat{x}_1 - \widehat{x}_2, \widehat{x}_2 - x^k \rangle$ , so that $l_1 - l_2 = -\|\widehat{x}_1 - \widehat{x}_2\|^2$ . Similarly, taking $k_m \to \infty$ such that $x^{k_m} \rightharpoonup \widehat{x}_2$ , $l_1 - l_2 = \| \widehat{x}_1 - \widehat{x}_2\|^2$ . Consequently, $\|\widehat{x}_1 - \widehat{x}_2\| = 0$ [so all weak cluster points coincide; every subsequence has a further weakly convergent subsequence with this same limit, which implies weak convergence of the whole sequence to that point] .

items.name: Yosida approximation of a maximal monotone operator
items.statement:
For a maximal monotone operator $A:H\Rightarrow H$ and $\lambda>0$, its Yosida approximation is the single-valued map $A_{\lambda}:H\to H$ defined by

$$
A_{\lambda}(x):=\frac{1}{\lambda}(x-J_{\lambda}^{A}(x)).
$$
Equivalently, if $\xi=x-J_{\lambda}^{A}(x)$, then $\xi/\lambda\in A(x-\xi)$.

items.name: Weak-strong closedness of maximal monotone graphs
items.statement: Let $A:H\Rightarrow H$ be maximal monotone. If $x_i\rightharpoonup x$ weakly in $H$, $v_i\to v$ strongly in $H$, and $v_i\in A(x_i)$ for all $i$, then $v\in A(x)$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{gra} A$ is closed in $H\times H$ for the weak-strong topology.
items.proof: Cited from: H. Brezis, Opérateurs maximaux monotones et semi-groupes de contractions dans les espaces de Hilbert, Mathematics Studies 5, North-Holland, Amsterdam, 1973. The paper invokes this result as “the graph of the maximal monotone operator A is closed in $H\times H$ for the weak-strong topology (see [7])” to pass to the limit in (2.13) and (3.11).

items.name: THEOREM 2.2
items.statement:
Let $(x^{k})\subset H$ be a sequence generated by (2.1)-(2.4), where $A:H\Rightarrow H$ is a maximal monotone operator with $S:= A^{-1}(\{0\})
eq\emptyset$ , $\sigma\in[0,1)$ , and the parameters $\alpha_{k}$ and $ho_{k}$ satisfy (1.4) and (1.6), respectively. Under (1.5), the following hold:

(i) For all $ ar{x} \in S$ , $\|x^{k} -  ar{x}\|$ is convergent, and

$$
\lim _ {k 	o \infty} \| x ^ {k + 1} - z ^ {k} / ho_ {k} - (1 - 1 / ho_ {k}) y ^ {k} \| = 0. 	ag {2.5}
$$

(ii) If in addition $\lambda_{k}$ satisfies (1.3), then $\lim_{k	o \infty}\| v^k\| = 0$ and there exists $x^{*}\in S$ such that $x^{k}ightharpoonup x^{*}$ weakly in $H$ as $k	o \infty$ .
items.proof:
Proof. From now on, assume that $v^k 
eq 0$ for all $k \geq 1$ ; otherwise, the algorithm finishes in a finite number of iterations, providing a solution to (1.1).

Let $ ar{x} \in S = A^{-1}(\{0\})$ and define $\varphi_k :=  rac{1}{2} \|x^k -  ar{x}\|^2$ . It follows from (2.4) that

$$
 egin{array}{l} \varphi_ {k + 1} =  rac {1}{2} \| y ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| ^ {2} + ho_ {k} \langle P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k}, y ^ {k} -  ar {x} angle +  rac {ho_ {k} ^ {2}}{2} \| P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k} \| ^ {2} \ =  rac {1}{2} \| y ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| ^ {2} - ho_ {k} \| P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k} \| ^ {2} + ho_ {k} \left\langle P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k}, P _ {k} y ^ {k} -  ar {x} ightangle +  rac {ho_ {k} ^ {2}}{2} \| P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k} \| ^ {2} \ =  rac {1}{2} \| y ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| ^ {2} - ho_ {k} (1 - ho_ {k} / 2) \| P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k} \| ^ {2} + ho_ {k} \langle P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k}, P _ {k} y ^ {k} -  ar {x} angle . \ \end{array}
$$

Next, notice that, by Lemma 2.1(i), $v^{k} 
eq 0$ implies $(y^{k} - z^{k}) / \lambda_{k} 
eq 0$ due to (2.1) and (2.2). Then, by virtue of Lemma 2.1(ii),

$$
\ell_ {k} (y ^ {k}) = \langle v ^ {k}, y ^ {k} - z ^ {k} angle \geq (1 - \sigma) \| v ^ {k} \| \| y ^ {k} - z ^ {k} \| > 0, 	ag {2.6}
$$

where $\ell_k(x) = \langle v^k, x - z^k angle$ . As $v^k \in ho_k A(z^k / ho_k + (1 - 1 / ho_k)y^k)$ , the monotonicity of $A$ gives $\langle v^k,  ar{x} - z^k / ho_k - (1 - 1 / ho_k)y^k angle \leq 0$ . Thus [multiplying the monotonicity inequality by $ho_k>0$ gives $\ell_k( ar{x})\leq(1-1/ho_k)\ell_k(y^k)$], $ ar{x}$ belongs to the half-space $H_k^\leq = \{x \in H \mid \ell_k(x) \leq (1 - 1 / ho_k)\ell_k(y^k)\}$ . Therefore, since $ho_k > 0$ and taking into account (2.6), the hyperplane $H_k$ given by (2.3) strictly separates $y^k$ from $ ar{x}$ . Moreover, since the orthogonal projection of $y^k$ onto $H_k$ is also the orthogonal projection onto the half-space $H_k^\leq$ , one gets $\langle P_k y^k - y^k, P_k y^k -  ar{x} angle \leq 0$ . It follows that

$$
\varphi_ {k + 1} \leq  rac {1}{2} \| y ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| ^ {2} - ho_ {k} (1 - ho_ {k} / 2) \| P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k} \| ^ {2}. 	ag {2.7}
$$

But $ rac{1}{2}\| y^k - ar{x}\|^2 = \varphi_k + \alpha_k\langle x^k - ar{x},x^k -x^{k - 1}angle + rac{\alpha_k^2}{2}\| x^k -x^{k - 1}\|^2$ . On the other hand, it is direct to verify that [using $\|a\|^2-\|b\|^2=2\langle a,a-bangle-\|a-b\|^2$ with $a=x^k- ar{x}$ and $b=x^{k-1}- ar{x}$] $\varphi_{k} = \varphi_{k - 1} + \langle x^{k} -  ar{x},x^{k} - x^{k - 1}angle - rac{1}{2}\| x^{k} - x^{k - 1}\|^{2}$ . Hence

$$
 rac {1}{2} \| y ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| ^ {2} = \varphi_ {k} + \alpha_ {k} (\varphi_ {k} - \varphi_ {k - 1}) +  rac {\alpha_ {k} + \alpha_ {k} ^ {2}}{2} \| x ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2}. 	ag {2.8}
$$

Thus

$$
\varphi_ {k + 1} \leq \varphi_ {k} + \alpha_ {k} (\varphi_ {k} - \varphi_ {k - 1}) + \delta_ {k} - ho_ {k} (1 - ho_ {k} / 2) \| P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k} \| ^ {2}, 	ag {2.9}
$$

where $\delta_k :=  rac{\alpha_k + \alpha_k^2}{2} \|x^k - x^{k-1}\|^2$ , which satisfies $\sum \delta_k < \infty$ thanks to (1.5) (recall that $\alpha_k \in [0,1)$ ).

By virtue of Lemma 2.3 applied to (2.9), the sequence $(\varphi_k)$ is convergent under (1.4) and (1.5). Since $ ar{x} \in S$ is arbitrary, the latter proves the first assertion in Theorem 2.2(i).

On the other hand, by Lemma 2.3(i), it follows from (2.9) that

$$
\sum ho_ {k} (1 - ho_ {k} / 2) \| P _ {k} y ^ {k} - y ^ {k} \| ^ {2} \leq \varphi_ {1} + \alpha \sum [ \varphi_ {k} - \varphi_ {k - 1} ] _ {+} + \sum \delta_ {k} <   \infty ,
$$

which amounts to

$$
(1 / R _ {2} - 1 / 2) \sum (\langle v ^ {k}, y ^ {k} - z ^ {k} angle / \| v ^ {k} \|) ^ {2} <   \infty , 	ag {2.10}
$$

with $R_{2} = \sup_{k\geq 1}ho_{k} < 2$ thanks to (1.6). By Lemma 2.1, it may be concluded from (2.10) that [Lemma 2.1(ii) gives $(1-\sigma)\|v^k\|\|y^k-z^k\|\leq\langle v^k,y^k-z^kangle$, while Lemma 2.1(i) applied to $u=(y^k-z^k)/\lambda_k$ gives $\lambda_k\|v^k\|\leq\|y^k-z^k\|/(1-\sigma)$]

$$
\sum \lambda_ {k} ^ {2} \| v ^ {k} \| ^ {2} \leq \sum \| y ^ {k} - z ^ {k} \| ^ {2} / (1 - \sigma) ^ {2} <   \infty . 	ag {2.11}
$$

It follows that

$$
\lim _ {k 	o \infty} \langle v ^ {k}, y ^ {k} - z ^ {k} angle / \| v ^ {k} \| = \lim _ {k 	o \infty} \| y ^ {k} - z ^ {k} \| = \lim _ {k 	o \infty} \lambda_ {k} \| v ^ {k} \| = 0. 	ag {2.12}
$$

By (2.4), the first limit in (2.12) ensures that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\|x^{k+1}-y^{k}\|=0$ . From this fact, together with the second limit in (2.12), it follows that (2.5) holds because $R_{1}=\infho_{k}>0$ due to (1.6). This completes the proof of Theorem 2.2(i).

In order to prove Theorem 2.2(ii), the idea is to apply the following well-known result on weak convergence in Hilbert spaces, whose proof is given here for the convenience of the reader.

By Theorem 2.2(i), condition (a) of Lemma 2.4 holds with $S = A^{-1}(\{0\})$ . Next, suppose (1.3) and let $\hat{x}$ be a weak cluster point of $(x^k)$ . By (2.5), $z^k / ho_k + (1 - 1 / ho_k)y^k ightharpoonup \hat{x}$ [along the chosen weakly convergent subsequence, since $x^{k+1}-y^k	o0$ and $x^{k+1}-(z^k/ho_k+(1-1/ho_k)y^k)	o0$ strongly] . But

$$
v ^ {k} / ho_ {k} \in A (z ^ {k} / ho_ {k} + (1 - 1 / ho_ {k}) y ^ {k}), 	ag {2.13}
$$

with $v^{k}/ho_{k} ightarrow 0$ strongly in H thanks to the last limit in (2.12) together with (1.3) and (1.6). Since the graph of the maximal monotone operator A is closed in $H 	imes H$ for the weak-strong topology (see [7]), it is possible to pass to the limit in (2.13) to deduce that $0 \in A(\hat{x})$ , i.e., $\hat{x} \in S$ . Thus, condition (b) of Lemma 2.4 is also satisfied, which proves the weak convergence of $(x^{k})$ . ☐

items.name: Remark 1
items.statement:
If (1.3) is replaced with

$$
\sum \lambda_ {k} ^ {2} = \infty , 	ag {2.14}
$$

then it may be deduced from (2.11) that there exists a subsequence of $(v^{k})$ that converges strongly to 0. In the finite dimensional case, this is sufficient for the convergence of $(x^{k})$ (see [23, Rem. 2.3]). Indeed, take $v^{k_{i}} ightarrow 0$ and assume that $\dim H < \infty$ . By Theorem 2.2(i), $(x^{k})$ is bounded so that one may assume that, up to a subsequence, $x^{k_{i} + 1}	o \hat{x}$ for some $\hat{x}\in H$ . By virtue of (2.5), one may let $k_{i}ightarrow \infty$ in (2.13) to deduce that $0\in A(\hat{x})$ . Hence $\hat{x}\in S$ and, by Theorem 2.2(i), $\| x^k -\hat{x}\|$ is convergent. Therefore $\lim_{k	o \infty}\| x^k -\hat{x}\| = \lim_{i	o \infty}\| x^{k_i + 1} - \hat{x}\| = 0$ .

items.name: PROPOSITION 2.5
items.statement:
Under the assumptions of Theorem 2.2 with, in addition, $(\alpha_{k})$ being nondecreasing (i.e., $\alpha_{k+1} \geq \alpha_{k}$ ) and satisfying $0 \leq \alpha_{k} \leq \alpha$ for some $\alpha \in [0,1)$ such that

$$
0 <   p (\alpha) := 1 / R _ {2} - 1 / 2 - (2 / R _ {1} - 1 / 2) \alpha - (1 - 1 / R _ {2}) \alpha^ {2}, 	ag {2.15}
$$

then $\sum \| x^k - x^{k-1} \|^2 < \infty$ . In particular, (1.5) holds and thus there exists $\widehat{x} \in S$ such that $x^k ightharpoonup \widehat{x}$ weakly in $H$ as $k 	o \infty$ .
items.proof:
Proof. Noticing that [substitute $y^k=x^k+\alpha_k(x^k-x^{k-1})$ and use $-2\langle a,bangle\geq-\|a\|^2-\|b\|^2$ in the weighted form] $ho_k^2 \| P_ky^k - y^k\|^2 = \| x^{k+1} - y^k\|^2 = \| x^{k+1} - x^k\|^2 - 2\alpha_k \langle x^{k+1} - x^k, x^k - x^{k-1} angle + \alpha_k^2 \| x^k - x^{k-1}\|^2 \geq (1 - \alpha_k)\| x^{k+1} - x^k\|^2 - \alpha_k(1 - \alpha_k)\| x^k - x^{k-1}\|^2$ , it follows from (2.9) that

$$
 egin{array}{l} \varphi_ {k + 1} \leq \varphi_ {k} + \alpha_ {k} (\varphi_ {k} - \varphi_ {k - 1}) + [ (\alpha_ {k} + \alpha_ {k} ^ {2}) / 2 + (1 / ho_ {k} - 1 / 2) \alpha_ {k} (1 - \alpha_ {k}) ] \| x ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2} \ - (1 / ho_ {k} - 1 / 2) (1 - \alpha_ {k}) \| x ^ {k + 1} - x ^ {k} \| ^ {2}, \ \end{array}
$$

where $\varphi_{k}:= rac{1}{2}\|x^{k}- ar{x}\|^{2}$ . This yields

$$
 egin{array}{l} \varphi_ {k + 1} - \alpha_ {k} \varphi_ {k} \leq \varphi_ {k} - \alpha_ {k} \varphi_ {k - 1} + \alpha_ {k} [ 1 / ho_ {k} + (1 - 1 / ho_ {k}) \alpha_ {k} ] \| x ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| ^ {2} \ - (1 / ho_ {k} - 1 / 2) (1 - \alpha_ {k}) \| x ^ {k + 1} - x ^ {k} \| ^ {2}. \ \end{array}
$$

Setting $\mu_k := \varphi_k - \alpha_k \varphi_{k-1} + \alpha_k [1/ho_k + (1-1/ho_k) \alpha_k] \|x^k - x^{k-1}\|^2$ , and since $\alpha_{k+1} \geq \alpha_k$ [so the term $-\alpha_{k+1}\varphi_k$ is no larger than $-\alpha_k\varphi_k$ after moving to the left-hand side] , we obtain

$$
\mu_ {k + 1} \leq \mu_ {k} + [ \alpha_ {k + 1} / ho_ {k + 1} + (1 - 1 / ho_ {k + 1}) \alpha_ {k + 1} ^ {2} + (1 / ho_ {k} - 1 / 2) (\alpha_ {k} - 1) ] \| x ^ {k + 1} - x ^ {k} \| ^ {2}.
$$

But $\alpha_{k + 1} / ho_{k + 1} + (1 - 1 / ho_{k + 1})\alpha_{k + 1}^2\leq \alpha /R_1 + (1 - 1 / R_2)\alpha^2$ and $(1 / ho_k - 1 / 2)(\alpha_k - 1)\leq (1 / R_1 - 1 / 2)\alpha -1 / R_2 + 1 / 2$ . Therefore $\mu_{k + 1}\leq \mu_k - p(\alpha)\| x^{k + 1} - x^k\|^2$ , where $p(\alpha)$ is given by (2.15). Since $p(\alpha) > 0$ , $(\mu_k)$ is nonincreasing, which implies $\varphi_{k}\leq \alpha \varphi_{k - 1} + \mu_{k}\leq \alpha \varphi_{k - 1} + \mu_{1}$ . This gives $\varphi_{k}\leq \alpha^{k}\varphi_{0} + \mu_{1}\sum_{j = 0}^{k - 1}\alpha^{j}\leq \alpha^{k}\varphi_{0} + \mu_{1} / (1 - \alpha)$ . Furthermore, it follows that $p(\alpha)\sum_{j = 0}^{k}\| x^{j + 1} - x^{j}\|^2\leq \mu_{1} - \mu_{k + 1}\leq \mu_{1} + \alpha \varphi_{k}\leq \alpha^{k + 1}\varphi_{0} + \mu_{1} / (1 - \alpha)$ . This shows that $\sum \| x^k -x^{k - 1}\|^2\leq 2\mu_1 / ((1 - \alpha)p(\alpha))$ [after taking the supremum over the partial sums and absorbing the bounded geometric tail] . The conclusion follows by Theorem 2.2.

items.name: Remark 2
items.statement: Suppose $R_{2} \geq 1$ . Since $p(0) = 1 / R_{2} - 1 / 2 > 0$ thanks to (1.6), there exists a unique positive root $\alpha^{*} > 0$ of the quadratic polynomial $p(\alpha)$ , and for all $\alpha \in [0, \alpha^{*})$ , $p(\alpha) > 0$ . For instance, when $\rho_{k} \equiv 1$ , one gets $p(\alpha) = 1 / 2 - (3 / 2)\alpha$ and so $\alpha^{*} = 1 / 3$ .

items.name: THEOREM 3.1
items.statement:
Let $A:H\Rightarrow H$ be a maximal monotone operator with $S:= A^{-1}(\{0\})
eq\emptyset$ and $(x^{k})\subset H$ a sequence satisfying

$$
(x ^ {k + 1} - y ^ {k}) / \lambda_ {k} + v ^ {k} = \eta^ {k} \quad 	ext {for some} v ^ {k} \in ho_ {k} A (x ^ {k + 1} / ho_ {k} + (1 - 1 / ho_ {k}) y ^ {k}), 	ag {3.2}
$$

where $y^{k} = x^{k} + \alpha_{k}(x^{k} - x^{k - 1})$ , and the parameters $\lambda_{k}$ , $\alpha_{k}$ , and $ho_{k}$ satisfy (1.3), (1.4), and (1.6), respectively. Suppose (1.5), (3.1), and

$$
\sum \lambda_ {k} \| \eta^ {k} \| \| y ^ {k} \| <   \infty . 	ag {3.3}
$$

Then $v^k 	o 0$ strongly in $H$ and there exists $x^* \in S$ such that $x^k ightharpoonup x^*$ weakly in $H$ .
items.proof:
Proof. It is easy to see that (3.2) amounts to [rewrite (3.2) as $y^k+(\lambda_k/ho_k)\eta^k\in (I+\lambda_kA)(x^{k+1}/ho_k+(1-1/ho_k)y^k)$ and then apply the resolvent definition]  $x^{k + 1} = (1 - ho_k)y^k +ho_kJ_{\lambda_k}^A (y^k +(\lambda_k / ho_k)\eta^k)$ . Let $(w^{k})$ be the auxiliary sequence defined by

$$
w ^ {k} := (1 - ho_ {k}) y ^ {k} + ho_ {k} J _ {\lambda_ {k}} ^ {A} (y ^ {k}). 	ag {3.4}
$$

Since $J_{\lambda}^{A}$ is nonexpansive,

$$
\| x ^ {k + 1} - w ^ {k} \| \leq \lambda_ {k} \| \eta^ {k} \|. 	ag {3.5}
$$

On the other hand, (3.4) may be written as $w^{k} = y^{k} - \lambda_{k}ho_{k}A_{\lambda_{k}}(y^{k})$ , where $A_{\lambda}:H	o H$ is given by $A_{\lambda} =  rac{1}{\lambda}(I - J_{\lambda}^{A})$ . Thanks to (1.2),

$$
0 \in A (x) 	ext {   if   and   only   if   } A _ {\lambda} (x) = 0. 	ag {3.6}
$$

Moreover, as $J_{\lambda}^{A}$ is nonexpansive, $A_{\lambda}$ is a cocoercive maximal monotone operator of parameter $\lambda$ ; that is,

$$
 orall x _ {1}, x _ {2} \in H, \langle A _ {\lambda} (x _ {1}) - A _ {\lambda} (x _ {2}), x _ {1} - x _ {2} angle \geq \lambda \| A _ {\lambda} (x _ {1}) - A _ {\lambda} (x _ {2}) \| ^ {2}. 	ag {3.7}
$$

Let $ ar{x} \in S$ . By (3.6), $A_{\lambda}( ar{x}) = 0$ and since $ rac{1}{2} \| w^k -  ar{x} \|^2 =  rac{1}{2} \| y^k -  ar{x} \|^2 - ho_k \lambda_k \langle y^k -  ar{x}, A_{\lambda_k}(y^k) angle +  rac{(ho_k \lambda_k)^2}{2} \| A_{\lambda_k}(y^k) \|^2$ , the cocoercivity property (3.7) yields

$$
 rac {1}{2} \| w ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| ^ {2} \leq  rac {1}{2} \| y ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| ^ {2} - \lambda_ {k} ^ {2} ho_ {k} (1 - ho_ {k} / 2) \| A _ {\lambda_ {k}} (y ^ {k}) \| ^ {2}. 	ag {3.8}
$$

Define $\varphi_{k}:= rac{1}{2}\|x^{k}- ar{x}\|^{2}$ . Then $\varphi_{k+1}\leq rac{1}{2}\|w^{k}- ar{x}\|^{2}+\|x^{k+1}-w^{k}\|\|w^{k}- ar{x}\|+ rac{1}{2}\|x^{k+1}-w^{k}\|^{2}$ . By (3.5) and (3.8),

$$
\varphi_ {k + 1} \leq  rac {1}{2} \| y ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| ^ {2} - \lambda_ {k} ^ {2} ho_ {k} (1 - ho_ {k} / 2) \| A _ {\lambda_ {k}} (y ^ {k}) \| ^ {2} + \lambda_ {k} \| \eta^ {k} \| \| y ^ {k} -  ar {x} \| +  rac {\lambda_ {k} ^ {2}}{2} \| \eta^ {k} \| ^ {2}. 	ag {3.9}
$$

Recalling (2.8), it follows that

$$
\varphi_ {k + 1} \leq \varphi_ {k} + \alpha_ {k} (\varphi_ {k} - \varphi_ {k - 1}) + \delta_ {k} - \lambda_ {k} ^ {2} ho_ {k} (1 - ho_ {k} / 2) \| A _ {\lambda_ {k}} (y ^ {k}) \| ^ {2}, 	ag {3.10}
$$

where $\delta_k :=  rac{\alpha_k + \alpha_k^2}{2} \|x^k - x^{k-1}\|^2 + \lambda_k\|\eta^k\|\|y^k -  ar{x}\| +  rac{\lambda_k^2}{2}\|\eta^k\|^2$ . Under (1.5), (3.1), if (3.3) holds, then $\sum \delta_k < \infty$ [because $\|y^k- ar{x}\|\leq\|y^k\|+\| ar{x}\|$, (3.3) controls the $\|y^k\|$ part, (3.1) controls the constant part, and boundedness of $(\lambda_k)$ from (3.1) makes $\sum\lambda_k^2\|\eta^k\|^2$ summable after discarding finitely many zero terms] . Thus $\sum \delta_k < \infty$ and, by virtue of Lemma 2.3, $(\varphi_k)$ is convergent. Moreover, we deduce that $\sum \lambda_k^2\|A_{\lambda_k}(y^k)\|^2 < \infty$ [by summing (3.10) as in the proof of (2.10), using Lemma 2.3(i) and the lower bound $ho_k(1-ho_k/2)\geq R_1(1-R_2/2)>0$] . Set $\xi^k := y^k - J_{\lambda_k}^A(y^k)$ , which amounts to

$$
\xi^ {k} / \lambda_ {k} \in A (y ^ {k} - \xi^ {k}). 	ag {3.11}
$$

Since $\sum \| \xi^k\|^2 < \infty$ [because $\xi^k=\lambda_k A_{\lambda_k}(y^k)$], in particular $\lim_{k	o \infty}\xi^k = 0$ . Let $\hat{x}$ be a weak cluster point of $(x^{k})$ . Since $\lim_{k	o \infty}\alpha_{k}\| x^{k} - x^{k - 1}\| = 0$ , $y^{k}ightharpoonup \hat{x}$ and consequently $y^{k} - \xi^{k}ightharpoonup \hat{x}$ . By the weak-strong closedness of the graph of $A$ , letting $k	o \infty$ in (3.11) gives $0\in A(\hat{x})$ . Therefore, condition (b) of Lemma 2.4 holds [condition (a) was obtained from the convergence of $\varphi_k$ for every $ ar{x}\in S$], which finishes the proof.

items.name: Remark 3
items.statement:
Under (1.5) and (3.1), assume

$$
\sum \alpha_ {k} \| x ^ {k} - x ^ {k - 1} \| <   \infty . 	ag {3.12}
$$

From (3.9), it follows that $\| x^{k+1} -  ar{x} \| \leq \| y^k -  ar{x} \| + \lambda_k \| \eta^k \| \leq \| x^k -  ar{x} \| + \alpha_k \| x^k - x^{k-1} \| + \lambda_k \| \eta^k \|$ . Using (3.1) and (3.12), $\| x^k -  ar{x} \|$ is convergent; in particular ( $y^k$ ) is bounded. Hence in view of (3.1), condition (3.3) is realized.
